fields.meta_title: Mental Health Landing Page Builder for Practices | Emergent
fields.meta_description: A mental health landing page turns a visit into a consultation request. See four practice examples and build one with a contact-only form.
fields.h1: Build a Mental Health Landing Page That Books Consultations
fields.hero_description: Build a mental health landing page that books consultation calls, with every request saved to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: Six Parts Between a Visitor and a Booked Call
fields.features_subheading: Each part does one job before the consultation call, and Emergent rewrites any of them when you send a new prompt.
fields.feature_1:
A form that asks for contact and timing

The form takes a name, a phone number or email, and the times that suit the visitor. Clinical questions wait for the intake paperwork that follows a booked consultation.
fields.feature_2:
Therapist bios placed beside the form

Each therapist gets a photo, the clients they work with, and the hours they keep. A visitor can choose a name from the bios, and the choice rides along with the request.
fields.feature_3:
Fees stated before anyone books

Put the session fee, the length of a session, and the payment options next to the form. Someone who reads them first arrives at the consultation call knowing the cost.
fields.feature_4:
A line that the form is not for emergencies

Set a short notice above the form saying requests are read during office hours only. Place the 988 Lifeline number in that same notice, where a visitor in crisis sees it first.
fields.feature_5:
Each request saved as a row you own

Every consultation request lands as a row in a database you own, with the time it arrived. The app emails the person who calls back, and you choose who that is in the prompt.
fields.feature_6:
Code you can take with you

Export the page and its request table to your GitHub repository on paid plans. Or keep it hosted on Emergent under your own domain, which uses credits, and change it by prompt.

fields.tab_content_1:
A first-available pick lands with Odessa

Wickmere Counseling Group lists four therapists, and its form asks each visitor to choose one or pick First available. A First available request emails Odessa Marlow, the intake coordinator, and she calls back with a match. This week 31 requests came in, and 12 of them picked First available.
fields.tab_content_2:
With 11 booked, five call times remain

Aldmoor Psychotherapy keeps two evenings a week for free 15-minute consultation calls, Tuesday and Thursday from 6 pm to 8 pm, 16 calls in all. The form lists only the times still open, and a time leaves the list once someone books it. This week 11 calls are booked, and the page shows the five call times left.
fields.tab_content_3:
When Juno frees a spot, 3 names get an email

Juno Ashby stopped taking new clients at Hartwell Pike Therapy when her caseload filled, and her page now takes waitlist names in place of booking requests. The list holds 23 people. When Juno marks an opening, the app emails the first 3 names on it.
fields.tab_content_4:
Each request says office or online

Every request at Penrose Mill Counseling carries one answer the front desk reads before calling back: sessions at the office on Mill Lane, or online. The answer is saved on the row. This month 46 requests came in, with 28 asking for online sessions and 18 for the office.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Mental Health Landing Page
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to a mental health landing page that books consultation calls and tells each visitor who will call back.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Pick the one booking the page asks for
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Say who the practice works with
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Label every field in plain words
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Name who calls back, and by when
fields.howto_step_1_des: Choose between a free consultation call and a first full session, and build the page around that one choice. A visitor who clicked an ad for a consultation should find the consultation, its length, and one button that books it.
fields.howto_step_2_des: List the ages and the session types the practice offers, such as adults and couples, or teens booked by a parent. A visitor who is not a fit learns it before filling in the form, and the intake coordinator gets fewer requests to turn down.
fields.howto_step_3_des: WCAG 3.3.2 reads: labels or instructions are provided when content requires user input. Write each label as a short phrase a visitor can answer at a glance, such as Best number to call, and keep the label visible while they type.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Pick the person who returns each request and write the timing on the page, such as within one business day. Put that person's name in the prompt, and the email for every new request goes to them alone.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Write what happens after a request
fields.howto_step_5_des: Replace a bare thank-you with what happens next: who will call, and within how many days. Give the number the call will come from. Anyone who saves it knows to answer when that number rings.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Put the page on the practice's domain
fields.howto_step_6_des: Publish the page under the practice's own web address. The link in a directory listing or an ad then matches the name on the office door and the business card. Custom domains come included in Emergent, and each one uses credits.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Send a test request from a phone
fields.howto_step_7_des: Fill in the form on a phone, with the screen as narrow as a visitor's, and check that the right person gets the email. Then open the request table and confirm the row holds every answer, including the time the visitor chose.

faq_plan.q: What is a mental health landing page?
faq_plan.a: A mental health landing page is a single web page that asks a visitor to book one thing with a therapy practice, such as a free consultation call. It pairs that offer with the fee and a short form, and leaves clinical questions to the intake that comes after booking.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a mental health landing page?
faq_plan.a: Write a prompt that names the practice, its therapists, the booking the page takes, and who calls each visitor back, then give it to Emergent's AI landing page builder. Emergent builds the page with a request table behind it. To change a field or a heading later, send another prompt.

faq_plan.q: What should therapist landing page design put on the first screen?
faq_plan.a: The practice name, the one booking the page offers, and the button that books it. Add a real photo of the therapist or the office in place of stock art. Keep the colors quiet and the type large enough to read on a phone, and move bios and fees further down.

faq_plan.q: How many fields should the form on a therapy landing page have?
faq_plan.a: Four or five. Ask how to reach the visitor, when they can talk, and which therapist or session type they want, then stop. Clinical history belongs in intake, after the consultation is booked. The form on the chiropractic landing page keeps to the same rule and leaves health questions out of the booking step.

faq_plan.q: Should a mental health landing page tell visitors where to get help in a crisis?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Next to the form, say when the practice reads new requests, and give the 988 Lifeline beside that line. The Lifeline's own site states: The 988 Lifeline is available 24/7/365. It adds that people can call, text, or chat with a 988 Lifeline counselor.

faq_plan.q: Should a mental health landing page show session fees?
faq_plan.a: Yes, when the practice charges set prices. Put the fee and the session length beside the form, and say whether a sliding scale exists. A visitor who has read the price before booking spends the consultation call on fit instead of cost.

faq_plan.q: How should a mental health landing page handle insurance?
faq_plan.a: Ask how the visitor will pay before anything else: insurance or self-pay. A visitor who picks insurance then sees the plans the practice is in network with, and member details wait for intake. The insurance example on the dentist landing page asks the same question first and shows each group its own next line.

faq_plan.q: What should a mental health landing page say when a therapist is not taking new clients?
faq_plan.a: Say it at the top, in one plain sentence, and offer a waitlist in place of the booking form. Tell visitors how often the practice reviews the list and how it contacts people. Requests from a page Emergent builds are stored in a database you own, and the list moves with the practice.

faq_plan.q: How do I write therapist bios for a mental health landing page?
faq_plan.a: Write each bio in the therapist's own voice, in four or five sentences about who they work with and how a first session runs. Add a recent photo and put credentials in one line at the end. Emergent builds a bio card for each therapist from your prompt and adds another when you ask.

faq_plan.q: Does a mental health landing page need a web designer?
faq_plan.a: No, not for the first version. Publish a page with your own copy first, and see whether consultation requests come in before paying for custom design. Emergent's free tier covers building and publishing. If you hire a studio later, read its design agency landing page and look for a past client site with a booking form.

plan.angle: Searchers for mental health landing page get design galleries, stock vectors and template stores that show how a calm page looks, never how a consultation request travels from the page to the person who calls back. This page shows four practice pages built around booking logistics only (a therapist picker in a group practice, a capped week of free consultation calls, a waitlist while a solo caseload is full, an office or online choice saved with each request), each with the form, the routing and the database row behind it, and gives a practice owner the build steps: one booking per page, a contact-only form that leaves clinical questions to intake, fees stated before the form, and a plain line that the form is not for emergencies with the 988 Lifeline beside it. It makes no treatment, outcome, diagnosis, crisis-care or privacy-law claims. Telehealth, chiropractic and dentist pages are siblings and stay out of the headings.

scope.evidence: Builder scope throughout: 'Build a mental health landing page that books consultation calls'; plan rules out treatment, outcome, diagnosis, crisis-care and privacy-law claims, and none appear (no HIPAA, no therapy outcomes).

intent.evidence: Examples (four practice tabs), a seven-step how-to and design FAQ ('What should therapist landing page design put on the first screen?') serve the gallery/template top 10 with the booking-logistics angle.

specificity.evidence: 'Tuesday and Thursday from 6 pm to 8 pm, 16 calls in all' (4 hours of 15-minute calls = 16); 'A First available request emails Odessa Marlow, the intake coordinator'.

openers.evidence: Tab openers are scenes: 'Wickmere Counseling Group lists four therapists', 'Juno Ashby stopped taking new clients at Hartwell Pike Therapy'.

craft.evidence: Steps are concrete: 'Fill in the form on a phone, with the screen as narrow as a visitor's, and check that the right person gets the email.'

voice.evidence: Plain, practice-owner voice: 'Clinical questions wait for the intake paperwork that follows a booked consultation.' Repetition of 'request' logged as a note.

truth.evidence: 988 quote word for word from domain_sources: 'The 988 Lifeline is available 24/7/365.'; call/text/chat paraphrase matches the second span. WCAG 3.3.2 quoted exactly and scoped to labels: 'labels or instructions are provided when content requires user input'. Emergent claims map to claims_used (custom-domain 'each one uses credits', code-export 'on paid plans', free-start 'covers building and publishing').

distinct.evidence: Chiropractic, dentist and design agency pages appear only as FAQ links; no sibling primary in a heading.

faq.evidence: Ten builder-intent questions; Q2 carries the hub link; 'Should a mental health landing page tell visitors where to get help in a crisis?' answers with a sourced line and no crisis-care claim. Q1 PA7 flag awaits Divit and is not a finding.
